newsitem.title: USA: Hilton likely to bide time in raising offer.
newsitem.headline: Hilton likely to bide time in raising offer.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp will probably have to raise its $55 per share offer for ITT Corp to succeed in its takeover attempt, but investors should not expect such a move anytime soon, analysts said on Thursday.
Indeed, Hilton could wait until ITT's annual shareholders meeting to sweeten its offer. ITT has not scheduled an annual meeting yet, but it usually holds them in mid-May.
"At this point, I don't see why there's any reason they should (raise their offer). There's not a competing bid on the table," said Daniel Davila, an analyst at Rodman and Renshaw.

Still, ITT's shares have not dipped below Hilton's bid price since the hostile offer was launched on January 27. The stock closed up 5/8 at 58-1/4 on Thursday. Analysts say the final merger price could rise to about $65 a share.

"I don't think any rational person on Wall Street felt the Hilton bid was a last bid," said Marvin Roffman at Roffman, Miller Associates. "As a matter of fact, they came out on Day One and said this isn't necessarily their last bid. You don't say a thing like that unless you're going to up the bid."
To be sure, a move to sweeten the offer now would prove counterproductive as Hilton would be bidding against itself.
